title: The US army just detonated a poison bomb over Iowa | Steven Donziger
summary: The shocking situation in Iowa is a metaphor for much of what is wrong with the United States There’s no way to hide it: the US government just deliberately detonated a poison bomb of lead azide over the state of Iowa when a totally safe alternative was available. The problem in Iowa was relatively simple to solve. The army for decades had stored lead underground at a munitions facility. As far back as 2009, the government knew the lead was deteriorating and might blow up on its own. But it procrastinated. Finally, in March, the army hired a Georgia-based company to use a chemical spray to neutralize the lead, creating a non-hazardous byproduct that can be disposed of in landfills. Steven Donziger is a US-based human rights and environmental lawyer and the author of Donziger On Justice on Substack Continue reading...

title: Trump is destroying the rule of law in the US – to protect himself and the tech titans he worships as new gods | Jonathan Freedland
summary: To get Jensen Huang back at Nvidia, the president trampled on the justice system, national security and the trust America needs to do business in the global economy Don’t let the sex distract you. Or the lies or the boardroom intrigue or even the AI-generated bra, all of which could have come from an especially wild episode of Succession. Don’t let that lure you into thinking that the Jensen Huang affair is, as Donald Trump would have it, little more than a sex scandal involving a corporate maestro. It is much more serious than that. The events of the past week tell instead a story of legal immunity and indeed impunity – revealing how Trump is putting himself, the tech bros and even artificial intelligence above the law. It can be hard to see that through the thicket of questions that surround this episode, each one of which, don’t get me wrong, merits attention. Consider the personal profit Trump made thanks to his re-installation of Huang as the CEO of Nvidia, the world’s leading maker of advanced AI chips. Breaking the norm observed by previous presidents who, keen to avoid even the appearance of a conflict of interest, either divested themselves of stock holdings or placed them in a blind trust, Trump cheerfully buys and sells stocks in companies whose fates he can influence. He saw the value of his shares in Nvidia plunge when Huang was forced out, following revelations that the CEO had had an affair with Alice Huang, reportedly an asset of Chinese intelligence. Last weekend Trump urged the board to reconsider; Huang was reinstated on Monday and Nvidia’s value promptly soared – putting $15m in Trump’s pocket . Not for the first time, he had used the power of his office to enrich himself. Jonathan Freedland is a Guardian columnist Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? title: The explosion of extreme wealth is the major problem of our time | Bernie Sanders
summary: At this pivotal moment in American history, let us move forward together to take on and defeat a powerful, greedy and corrupt ruling class We are at a pivotal moment in history. Never before in human history have so few people held so much wealth and so much power. And never before have we seen such an unprecedented level of greed, arrogance and irresponsibility on the part of the world’s ruling class. Here is the good news: leaders from around the world are finally starting to wake up. This week, elected officials and economists from around the world – including four Nobel prize winners – came together in Paris for a “Summit Against International Oligarchy”. As the summit’s proclamation stated, “The explosion of extreme wealth is the major social fact of our time … We are sounding the alarm: billionaires are a threat to our democracies.” Bernie Sanders is a US senator, and ranking member of the health, education, labor and pensions committee. He represents the state of Vermont and is the longest-serving independent in the history of Congress Continue reading...

title: Can Borussia Dortmund finally end their title wait? Three big questions for Bundesliga leaders
summary: Niko Kovac’s team lead the way and, with Bayern Munich wounded, have a golden chance to be German champions for the first time in 15 years Borussia Dortmund’s dreams have a habit of becoming nightmares, like when they somehow handed Bayern Munich the Bundesliga title on the final day of the 2022-23 season. Or when an 89th-minute Arjen Robben goal won the 2013 Champions League final for the same opponents. Whenever Dortmund suffer heartbreak, it usually involves Bayern. As things stand, however, Niko Kovac’s side hold a two-point lead over Bayern at the top of the Bundesliga. Both teams are unbeaten, but Dortmund may be the more stable of the two at the moment, especially with Harry Kane expected to miss several months through injury. Continue reading...

title: Trump Medicaid cuts will hit the most vulnerable Americans, officials say
summary: In Kentucky, one of America’s unhealthiest states, denial of healthcare and potential closure of hospitals may affect 250,000 people The coalfields of eastern Kentucky fueled America’s economic rise in the early 20th century. But the state has since found itself left behind. A lack of investments in rural regions has triggered health and socioeconomic issues that have lingered for generations. Today, Kentucky faces the third-highest cancer and third-highest drug overdose death rate in the country and is one of the top five worst-affected states in several other health metrics. It has come to rely heavily on federal healthcare assistance, with about 1.4 million people in Kentucky receiving Medicaid support. Continue reading...

title: Bills, Eagles and Bears pull off last-gasp wins in trio of Thanksgiving thrillers
summary: Bass hits from 57 yards at the gun to lift Buffalo Elliott’s 59-yarder caps Eagles’ 21-point comeback Bears take NFC North lead on Odunze’s late catch After sharing top billing, Buffalo’s Josh Allen and Kansas City’s Patrick Mahomes proved no match for the elements in the latest showdown of two of the NFL’s best quarterbacks. With both offense’s failing to gain traction on a rainy, windy and cold Thursday night, the Bills improved their AFC-leading record to 10-1 by slogging through a 13-10 victory over the visiting Chiefs on Tyler Bass’s 57-yard field goal as time expired. title: Jerry Jones hits out at Cowboys’ ‘damning setbacks’ after latest meltdown
summary: Owner still backs head coach after 39-38 loss to Eagles Brian Schottenheimer has overseen record skid at home Falcons rule out five players for game at Minnesota Jerry Jones has backed Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer after another meltdown in a 39-38 loss to Philadelphia on Thanksgiving, but the owner qualified his support by claiming “these are setbacks and they’re damning setbacks”. “I do,” Jones said when asked if he still believed his second-year coach could lead the Cowboys to a Super Bowl. “I do, but on the other hand, these are setbacks and they’re damning setbacks.” Continue reading...

title: Lights-out Luka Dončić and contagious chemistry: are these Lakers for real?
summary: It’s early days, but after a dramatic roster overhaul and an offseason of team-bonding Dončić is playing at an MVP level and LA are looking like contenders One of the components of Luka Dončić’s shock trade from the Dallas Mavericks to the Los Angeles Lakers that caused great consternation was that he was just entering his prime as an NBA superstar. The worry was that the move could end that prime before it really even began – unceremoniously uprooting the Slovenian wunderkind from a team custom built around his strengths, fresh off a run to the NBA finals, to one who didn’t really make sense at all. Sure, the bright lights of Hollywood would elevate Dončić’s profile and usher him into a new echelon of stardom. But with Oklahoma City starting their run of dominance and rising stars around the league waiting in the wings, some believed his hopes of title contention (or even a long-elusive MVP award) had vanished. But the start to this season raises the question: what if they were wrong? Dončić is neck-and-neck with Victor Wembanyama in the MVP race, and the Lakers have the best record in the NBA at 15-3, with the Spurs and 76ers just behind at 15-4. San Antonio and their gargantuan French superstar were title and MVP favorites by a wide margin entering this season. But Dončić and the Lakers are keeping pace by pretty much every margin. Friday night’s NBA Cup showdown will be a duel with ripple effects and stakes rarely seen in the regular season, let alone in November. The two top records. The two leading MVP candidates. A basketball fan couldn’t ask for much more. Continue reading...

title: Trump claims revised economic data shows pre-midterms figures were ‘fake’ | First Thing
summary: President calls for investigation after GDP figures were adjusted upwards, despite revisions to official economic figures being commonplace. Plus, the weird and macabre world of Victorian Christmas cards Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here Good morning. Donald Trump has alleged without evidence that economic figures published by the US federal government before this month’s midterm elections were “fake” and demanded an investigation after voters roundly rejected his Republican party. In a holiday message on his Truth Social platform, the US president wished a happy Thanksgiving “to even those who issued fake Economic Numbers, just prior to the Election, and corrected them yesterday, three weeks late, showing that the GDP was actually 4.3%, versus 3.4%”. Why did Trump call the figures fake? Revisions to official economic figures are commonplace, but Trump has tried repeatedly to challenge trust in economic data that does not support his claims that a historic boom is under way in the US. “Why wasn’t the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. “This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error”. What other acerbic well-wishes did Trump offer? He wished “a very Happy Thanksgiving to all of those people that have worked so hard to bring our Country to the Radical Far Left” as well as “those who want to redistribute Property, so that all of the hardworking people that have built up, over a lifetime, a certain Wealth, will now be forced to distribute it throughout the Country, even to those who refuse to work”. Why are the ballots at the center of an ongoing dispute over the 2020 election? Some Republicans, led by Trump, claimed the election results had been rigged despite Joe Biden being certified after several recounts. Republican state officials had refused to overturn the result, despite a now-infamous phone call from Trump to pressure the Georgia secretary of state, Brad Raffensperger, to “find 11,780 votes”. Continue reading...

title: Three studies link glyphosate to cancer, contradicting claims of Trump EPA
summary: Experts say NIH research raises concerns about chemical companies’ influence on US agency’s pesticide division The US government’s top medical research agency has released three new studies linking glyphosate, the world’s most widely used pesticide and an active ingredient in Roundup, to cancer . The National Institutes of Health (NIH) findings contradict a controversial recent Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) conclusion that the weedkiller is not a carcinogen, and deals a blow to the White House, which has been closely allied with Roundup’s producer, Bayer. The NIH’s three papers could have significant political and legal fallout. The EPA is in the process of a court-ordered re-evaluation of glyphosate’s cancer risks. The NIH findings generate new pressure for the EPA to find that the substance is linked to cancer, which would subject it to a modest increase in regulations. Continue reading...

The storms snarled travel, downed trees and power lines and led to water rescues from New York to Virginia. At its peak, nearly a million customers were without power . Continue reading...

title: Jared Kushner’s 70-minute interview reveals naive bias in handling of Putin’s aggression
summary: Trump’s son-in-law and senior negotiator paints Russian invasion of Ukraine as a misunderstanding to be resolved In the space of a 70-minute interview, Jared Kushner – Donald Trump’s son-in-law and a prominent US negotiator in Russia, Gaza and Iran – probably did more to reveal why the world is mired in entrenched conflicts than a thousand geopolitical tomes or seminars. During the conversation this week with Mathias Döpfner, the chief executive of the Axel Springer media publisher, Kushner gave a rare insight into his diplomatic technique, offering a string of homilies that veered close to banalities: “You have nothing until you have something”, “diplomacy is like untying knots on a fishing line for his son”, and “you play the ball from where it lands”. title: King tides batter US coasts as storms threaten Thanksgiving celebrations
summary: Heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding creating hazardous conditions for millions travelling for holiday King tides and huge waves have been battering both coasts of the US during a turbulent Thanksgiving period, with severe weather threatening millions across the country. Along the California coast, king tides caused considerable damage. In Pacifica, south of San Francisco, large waves battered the coastline on Wednesday, destroying part of a pier and sending debris into the ocean. The National Weather Service issued coastal flood warnings covering parts of the Pacific coastline and shorelines around San Francisco Bay and San Pablo Bay. Several beachfront properties in Pacifica have already experienced flooding, while authorities in Marin County temporarily issued an evacuation warning for residents of beachfront homes at Stinson Beach. Continue reading...

title: Newly released documents suggest CIA did more post-9/11 waterboarding than previously acknowledged
summary: Declassified documents appear to support belief that waterboarding was more common and may have occurred beyond two acknowledged sites Newly released documents suggest that the CIA waterboarded more detainees during the post-9/11 “war on terror” than previously acknowledged, utilizing a site north of Kabul, Afghanistan, for the practice of simulated drowning. The agency has acknowledged waterboarding three men: Abu Zubaydah, believed to be a high-ranking member of al-Qaida; Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, suspected architect of the 11 September 2001 attacks; and Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri, accused of planning the 2000 bombing of a navy destroyer. Local media reported that 18 people at the Leon medical center headquarters in Doral fell ill due to possible food poisoning after attending the center’s annual Thanksgiving lunch on Wednesday. title: ‘Abusive and insulting to Canadians’: campaign to oust US ambassador presented to parliament
summary: Hundreds of thousands of Canadians call for Pete Hoekstra to be declared ‘persona non grata’ A petition signed by nearly 290,000 Canadians calling on Mark Carney’s government to oust Pete Hoekstra as US ambassador to Canada was formally presented to the House of Commons on Thursday, a sign of the strained relations between the neighboring countries. Elizabeth May, a Canadian Green party member, originally opened the petition for signatures in July 2026 after a woman from Calgary sponsored it. The petition requests that the Canadian government declare Hoekstra “persona non grata” due to his “US” diplomatic interference in Canadian domestic affairs”. Continue reading...
